source: independent validator; fresh primary-page refetches and source snapshots
rejected: The hard part is where to release them. The supplied narration ranks this as the hardest challenge; no source makes that comparative assessment. Replace with a neutral location question.
A new USDA report from Kerrville. The source locates the quoted lab director in Kerrville; it does not establish where the report was authored. Attribute the statement to that lab director.

The model has a blind spot: people can transport infested animals. The research draft makes the limitation categorical. ARS says not every scenario is predictable, especially transport, rather than claiming every model excludes it.

A rancher can move animals when the defined quarantine restrictions are lifted. This candidate consequence requires all remaining movement conditions and exact zone geography. It is excluded from this short film; no zone-release claim is accepted here.
required_edits_applied: Bound the date claim to publication rather than an invented deployment date.
Bound Kerrville attribution to the named laboratory director.
Accepted only the limited transport-prediction statement.
Excluded zone-release and unrestricted-animal-movement claims from the verified claim set.
Replaced the unsupported difficulty ranking with the neutral release-location question.
Replaced ambiguous report geography with precise Kerrville lab-director attribution.
Bound every final narration scene to verified claims; all other storyboard fields were preserved.
Expanded every evidence excerpt to the complete supporting sentence or passage from the independently fetched snapshot; c6 was also bound to s2 for explicit sterile-fly terminology.

scene_findings.text: This fly is fought with more flies.
scene_findings.finding: SIT purpose supported. The phrase describes a control method without promising eradication.

scene_findings.text: Sterile males mate with wild females. Their eggs never hatch.
scene_findings.finding: Sterile male and wild female mating yields nonviable eggs. This is the biological mechanism, not a field success rate.

scene_findings.text: The next question is where to release them.
scene_findings.finding: Neutral editorial transition to release location, an explicitly documented model application. Prior unsupported ranking removed.

scene_findings.text: USDA's lab director in Kerrville says AI models already guide that choice.
scene_findings.finding: Precisely attributes existing model use to the quoted lab director in Kerrville. Prior report-origin ambiguity removed.

scene_findings.text: Habitat, weather and past outbreaks become clues to where screwworm could spread.
scene_findings.finding: Habitat suitability, temperature, precipitation and historical outbreaks are documented inputs. Could preserves predictive uncertainty.

scene_findings.text: That helps direct traps, surveillance and sterile insects.
scene_findings.finding: Existing surveillance, adult trapping and SIT placement use is explicitly reported by ARS.

scene_findings.text: The models can't predict every trip carrying an infested animal.
scene_findings.finding: Cannot predict every trip is a bounded paraphrase of the stated transport-related prediction limit; it does not claim all transport is unmodeled.

scene_findings.text: Livestock owners should check animals and report suspected cases. Never move an animal suspected of infestation.
scene_findings.finding: TAHC supports monitoring and immediate reporting. USDA explicitly prohibits moving suspected infested animals.

scene_findings.text: The forecast helps place the flies. People still have to stop the ride.
scene_findings.finding: Editorial synthesis of release-location guidance and the owner instruction. Board continuity retains the suspected-animal scenario from s8 and a closed loading gate; it does not forbid all animal movement.

numeric_scope: Only the sourced publication date is approved for numeric on-screen use. Do not display invented risk percentages, model accuracy or case totals.
visual_scope: Original labeled illustrations only; no invented actual forecast, measured release boundary, observed ranch footage or proof of eradication.
wording_scan: Zero prohibited whole-word matches in newly authored claim prose.

illustration_audit.basis: Authored scene descriptions and continuity, not a rendered-film inspection.
illustration_audit.sex_and_sterility_colors: Teal male and coral female are author-defined teaching colors. Identify their roles and display an illustration label; these colors are not diagnostic traits or evidence of sterility.
illustration_audit.nonhatch_sequence: Closed eggs correctly illustrate the cited nonviable-egg mechanism. No measured success percentage or claim that the whole wild population has stopped reproducing is approved.
illustration_audit.transport_sequence: A fictional owner observes a possible problem, reports it and stops a proposed trip; no diagnosis from color or a glance is asserted.
illustration_audit.forecast_sequence: Original conceptual landscape and target only; no measured risk surface, actual release polygon or geographical forecast is verified.
illustration_audit.render_review_required: Final judges must verify readable illustration labeling and that the intended limited claims survive the actual visual presentation.

internal_editorial_note: The director was notified that documentary.source_limit should say models cannot predict every animal-transport scenario. That board field was left untouched under the field-only edit instruction; final narration already uses the bounded form.

evidence_excerpt_audit.scope: Evidence passages support the full accepted statement, including publication context, model inputs, existing operational use and owner instructions.
